newsitem.title: UK: Courtaulds says Q1 pre-tax profits down.
newsitem.headline: Courtaulds says Q1 pre-tax profits down.

text.p: British chemicals group Courtaulds Plc said on Wednesday that the strong pound and increased interest charges has pulled its first quarter pre-tax profits "a little below" that of the corresponding period in the previous year.
Chairman David Lees told the annual general meeting that at comparable exchange rates operating profits were running ahead of last year and margins continued to improve.

"However, the effect of the strength of sterling on the translation of overseas profits is more pronounced than it was in the same period last year, and this, combined with increased interest charges as a consequence or our capital investment programme, has left profit before tax a little below the first quarter of 1998/97," Lees said in a statement.

Sterling has strengthened by 29 percent against the main European currencies since the first half of 1996/97, of which eight percent has been in the last two months. It said that while the movement against the dollar has been less dramatic, both are "adversely affecting trading competitiveness as well as profit translation."
Following changes to Advance Corporation Tax announced in the budget, Courtaulds does not expect to increase its pension contributions but said "there may be a small adverse effect on profits."
